title: Shortest Paths and Spanning Trees
welcome_lead: Find the cheapest route and the leanest network.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: Dijkstra's algorithm, Prim's and Kruskal's MST.
final_note: These three algorithms power maps, routing and design.

concepts.def: Finds shortest paths from a source in a non-negative weighted graph.
Minimum spanning tree — a cycle-free subgraph connecting all vertices at minimum total weight.
Builds an MST by growing from a starting vertex.
Builds an MST by adding cheapest edges that do not form a cycle.
A queue ordered by priority — used by Dijkstra and Prim.
An algorithm that takes the locally best step at each stage.

walkthroughs.body_html: Dijkstra (1959) finds shortest paths from a source. It picks the unvisited vertex with smallest tentative distance, relaxes its neighbours, and repeats. With a binary heap it runs in O((V+E) log V).
Both build a minimum spanning tree. Prim grows a tree from one vertex using a priority queue. Kruskal sorts edges and adds the cheapest that does not create a cycle, using a union-find structure.
Both MST algorithms are greedy: locally cheapest choices give the globally optimal tree, thanks to the cut property. Dijkstra is greedy too, provided weights are non-negative.
